document.title: Afghanistan: Taliban Take Shindand Air Base; Herat Threatened - Will Iran Intervene
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] Reports the Taliban seizure of Shindand Air Base, previously held by Ismail Khan, and their advance on Herat. Discusses possible Iranian reactions to the Taliban threat.

events.description: Taliban seize Shindand air base in Farah province.
Taliban front-line reportedly north of Adraskan, 30 km south of Herat airport; Taliban begin rocketing Masood's positions from Maidan Shahr.
Jumbesh under Rasul Pahlawan take Qala-i-Naw and press toward Herat.
Taliban front line reportedly north of Adraskan, 30 km south of Herat airport.
UNOCHA's Barber told POLOFF UN staff in Herat authorized to leave overland for Iran or Turkmenistan.
Jumbesh troops under Rasul Pahlawan took Qala-i-Naw, pressing toward Herat.
Pressure on Hekmatyar's Sarobi front diminished as Masood pulled troops back toward Kabul.
Taliban at Maidan Shahr began rocketing Masood's positions.
Dostam's officials announced no aircraft may overfly their territory without approval.

key_claims: Taliban seized Shindand airbase 3 Sep 1995 and were about 30 km from Herat airport.
Ismael Khan's position was weakened by reliance on Panjshiri troops and press-ganging.
Iranian intervention was seen as the key variable in whether Herat holds.
Jumbesh took Qala-i-Naw, adding pressure on Herat from the east.
A reported Zardad–Taliban deal in Wardak allowed Taliban to shell Masood from Maidan Shahr.
Dostam's forces restricted airspace over concern about arms deliveries to Kabul.
